Recorder
The Office of the County Recorder was created by the First Legislative Assembly of the Territory of Iowa in 1839. The County Recorder continues to maintain official records of documents affecting real estate in order to protect innocent third parties in real estate transactions. The County Recorder’s office is at the hub of the courthouse and functions to serve you. The County Recorder’s office has many additional duties and services it provides to the public.

Lands And Records Management
Expand
Your recorder/registrar is responsible for recording:
Deeds
Change of Titles
Affidavit of Surviving Spouse
Real Estate Contract
These documents need to have a Declaration of Value, Ground Water Hazard Statement, and payment of transfer tax when applicable
PLEASE INCLUDE A POSTAGE PAID, APPROPRIATE SIZED RETURN ENVELOPE FOR ALL YOUR RECORDED DOCUMENTS PLEASE.
Fees for recording the above documents are as follows:
$12.00 for first page
(+) $5.00 for each additional page
(+) $5.00 per parcel if more than one parcel is listed
Your recorder is also responsible for recording:
Mortgages
Extensions
Amendments / Modifications
Releases / Satisfactions
Assignments
Easements
Leases
Bill of Sales
Trade Names
Articles of Incorporation
Power of Attorney
Plats of Surveys
Corner Certificate
Affidavits (with no legal)
State/Federal Liens
Uniform Commercial Code (UCC) filing
Fees for recording the above are as follows:
$7.00 for the first page (Plats of Surveys)
$7.00 (All Others)
$5.00 for each additional page (All)
Military Discharge Papers
You may receive a copy of your military discharge (DD214) papers for no charge.
Certification fees are $5.00 for the first page and $0.50 for each additional page.
Searches
Our office is open to the public to come and do searches.
Our friendly staff is here to help guide you in your search for the records you desire.
If you are requesting our office to do a search, regarding land tracts, you will need the following information:
Names of who sold and who bought, if possible
Dates
Legal Description
Type of Document
Scan Number or Book and Page
Please allow us time in order to do the search. If you need copies, the cost is .50 cents per page. We need payment before the records can be mailed out to you.
Military Service Records
Expand
Discharge papers (DD214’s) may be recorded for permanent records and certified to perfect claims. In order to obtain a Certified copy the original document must be presented for recording. The DD214 must be recorded before military exemption is applied toward property tax reduction.
If the DD214 Military Discharge has been misplaced or destroyed, a certified copy may be obtained from the National Personnel Records Center in St. Louis, Missouri or other Custodian of Record listed on the Request Pertaining to Military Records form.
You may obtain the request form from the Emmet County Recorder’s Office.
You may receive a copy of your military discharge (DD214) papers for no charge. Certification fees are $5.00 for the first page and $0.50 for each additional page.
Vital Records
Expand
Certified copies of birth, death, and marriage can be obtained provided entitlement is proven. Certified copies are $20.00 each.
CALL FOR VITALS RECORDS, INCLUDING BIRTH, DEATH, & MARRIAGE PRIOR TO ARRIVAL TO VERIFY STAFF AVAILABILITY

Registers Birth Certificates
Registers Death Certificates

Birth, Marriage, & Death Certified Copies
All applications for certified copies of vital record events must be in writing and completely identify the record, as well as satisfactorily establish entitlement to the record being requested. Entitled persons include the person named on the record or that person’s spouse, children, legal parents, grandparents, grandchildren, siblings, or legal representative or guardian. A current government issued photo ID including the signature must be provided. Legal guardians, legal representatives, and siblings may be required to provide additional proof of entitlement.
Application for a certified copy requires a fee of $20.00 for the record search and includes one certified copy. Each additional copy of the same record is also $20.00. Fees are payable by cash, money order, or checks . Money orders and certified cashier’s checks must be made payable to “Emmet County Recorder”. You may pay with a credit/debit card (VISA or Mastercard) if you physically come into the office. There is an additional processing fee to use a credit/debit card. If applying through the mail you must include a copy of your current government issued photo ID, and the application must be notarized – signed in front of a Notary Public.
For a copy of the application or additional information, please contact the Emmet County Recorder’s Office at 712-362-4115.
Mail application, copy of valid government photo ID, notarized application, and payment to:
Emmet County Recorder
609 1st Ave N
Estherville, IA 51334
Death Records
The Recorders Office has official death registrations of Emmet County from 1880 to present. Also, Iowa statewide death certificates are now available from 1954 to present. All records are available for viewing during regular business hours. Record checks or verification of records over the telephone are not allowed per Iowa Code.
If you would like a certified copy of our county record, you must make a written application, provide photo ID, pay appropriate fee, and show satisfactory entitlement. Entitlement would include the person named on record, spouse, mother, father, brother, sister, child, legal guardian, or legal representative. Applicant must be 18 years of age.
Certified copies are available at $20.00 each to those persons with entitlement. Mail requests along with a money order to:
Emmet County Recorder
609 1st Ave N
Estherville, IA 51334
EXCEPTIONS: The records of deaths occurring between 1921 and 1941 can be obtained from the Iowa Department of Public Health through the Recorder’s Office Forward to State Process. Call 712-362-4115 .
Birth Records
The Recorders Office has official birth registrations of Emmet County from 1880 to present. Also, Iowa statewide birth records are now available from 1988 to present, however we do forward to states in our office, so we can do your processing for you, the record will just come from the state office if prior to that, and we will take the hassle out of your application. All records are available for viewing during regular business hours. Record checks or verification of records over the telephone are not allowed per Iowa Code.
If you would like a certified copy of our county record, you must make a written application, provide photo ID, pay appropriate fee, and show satisfactory entitlement. Entitlement would include the person named on record, spouse, mother, father, brother, sister, child, legal guardian, or legal representative. Applicant must be 18 years of age.
Certified copies are available at $20.00 each to those persons with entitlement. Please mail your requests along with a money order to:
Emmet County Recorder
609 1st Ave N
Estherville, IA 51334
Marriage Applications
The Recorders office is where you apply for a marriage license.
A marriage application cost is $35.00. The bride, groom and third party (age of 18), will all need to bring state issued, valid photo ID at time of application. Bride and groom will need to know how to spell parent’s full names, including mother’s maiden name.
If bride and/or groom are under 18 and older than 16, an application for minor will need to be signed by a parent or legal guardian. The bride and groom must appear before a judge and have this application signed.
There is a 3 day waiting period before actually getting the marriage certificate. The bride or groom can pick up the license and certificate of marriage after 3 business days. There is a three-day waiver form available for an additional $5.00 if the bride and groom need their license and certificate of marriage issued the same day. The bride and groom need to appear before a district judge for a signature on this waiver. This normally requires travel to a near by town, and an appointment with the judge.
The State of Iowa does not require blood tests.
After the ceremony the official will mail the completed Marriage Certificate to our office for filing within 15 days. We will then record it and make a certified copy and mail it to you.

Boat Registrations
Boats are renewed every (3) years. Boat owners should renew their boat licenses after January 1 and by April 30th to avoid penalty. Reminder ads will be printed in the local papers, no notices will be mailed.
Any vessel that is over 17 feet in length will need to be titled.
